Breakpoints for oopr

oopr_breakpoints.Rd

Set breakpoints for oopr classes.

Usage

OoprBreakpoints

Value

OoprBreakpoints

[private]
[4 fields] [2 methods]

Details

Breakpoints for oopr classes are set within the class object and all instances that are spawned from it.

When interacting with oopr breakpoints, changes to source files and their associated environment (either global or package) are checked for changes. This allows eligible breakpoints to be applied to classes that have been reloaded, and line numbers to be synced with the file.

OoprBreakpoints

Fields

rstudio

[static]
logical(1L)
Tap into RStudios breakpoint mechanism. See section RStudio below. Cannot be used with $volatile.

volatile

[static]
logical(1L)
Whether to automatically update breakpoints when changes to source files or environments occur. Updates only occur when this class is interacted with.

quiet

[static]
logical(1L)
Whether to silence messages when breakpoints auto update.

breaks

[read-only] [static]
data.frame(6L)
Currently set breakpoints; giving the file, class, name, line, steps, and condition. File paths are always relative to the current working directory. Lines displayed are referred to the last modified state of the file, not necessarily to a functions srcref.

Methods

add

[static]
Add breakpoints.

rm

[static]
Remove breakpoints.

add

Description

Add breakpoints.

Usage

add(file, lines, conds = list())

Arguments

filecharacter(1L)
Path to a .R file.
linesinteger()
Line numbers to add.
condslist()
A list of unevaluated expressions representing the condition of each breakpoint. Expressions must evaluate to logical(1L). Defaults to all lines being TRUE.

Details

If $volatile == TRUE, then lines must align with the most recent modified version of file.

Returns

this invisibly.

rm

Description

Remove breakpoints.

Usage

rm(file, lines = integer(0L))

Arguments

filecharacter(1L)
Path to a .R file.
linesinteger()
Line numbers to remove. The default unsets all lines.

Details

If $volatile == TRUE, then lines must align with the most recent modified version of file.

Returns

this invisibly.

RStudio

Setting breakpoints inside oopr classes is the same process as setting them for normal functions - use the gutter or SHIFT+F9.

RStudio calls its R functions inside tools:rstudio from the global environment. By assigning functions of the same name, these calls can be intercepted.

This feature is disabled by default as it is potentially destructive for an R session. Environmental variable R_OOPR_BREAKPOINTS=true can be used to enable this functionality when oopr namespace is loaded.

Breakpoints cannot be set on single line functions with a specifier,

get:x <- \( ) { return("x"); }

as RStudio thinks the line is at the top-level.

Tested with RStudio version 2026.1.1.403, there are no guarantees for earlier or later versions.

Examples

tmp <- tempfile();
on.exit(unlink(tmp));
cat(file = tmp, r"{
oopr("test",,
{
public:
  method <- \( )
  {
    "break me!";
  }
})
}");
source(tmp, keep.source = TRUE);
obj <- test();

OoprBreakpoints$add(tmp, 7L);
print(OoprBreakpoints);
#> <OoprBreakpoints ooprC: 0x55e3142d18e8>
#> Static Members:
#>  ├─$rstudio : logi FALSE
#>  ├─$volatile: logi TRUE
#>  ├─$quiet   : logi FALSE
#>  ├─$breaks  : ┬
#>  │            └─./../../../../../../../tmp/RtmpVHLJSp/file198377d3febf
#>  │              └─test
#>  │                └─method
#>  │                  └─7 [TRUE]
#>  │             
#>  ├─$add     :\(file, lines, conds = list())  
#>  └─$rm      :\(file, lines = integer(0L))  
if (FALSE) obj$method(); # \dontrun{}
